concepts.name: Types of Tariffs: Specific, Ad Valorem, and Compound Duties
key_dimensions: Distinction between specific duty (per unit) vs. ad valorem duty (% of value) and their revenue implications
Compound and mixed tariffs as hybrid instruments used in sensitive sectors
UPSC trap: Which type is MORE protective during price inflation — specific or ad valorem?
India's customs tariff structure under the Customs Tariff Act, 1975 and alignment with HSN codes

concepts.name: Effective Rate of Protection (ERP) vs. Nominal Tariff Rate
key_dimensions: ERP measures protection on value-added, not just on final goods — why it differs from nominal tariff
Tariff escalation: higher tariffs on processed goods vs. raw materials and its impact on industrialization in developing countries
UPSC trap: A low nominal tariff can coexist with a very high ERP — understanding the paradox
Policy implication: India's tariff structure criticized for inverted duty structure hurting domestic manufacturing

concepts.name: Inverted Duty Structure in India
key_dimensions: Definition: When import duty on raw materials/inputs is higher than on finished goods
Sectors affected: Electronics, textiles, chemicals — relevance to Make in India
Impact on domestic value addition and competitiveness of Indian manufacturers
Policy responses: PLI scheme, GST compensation, and periodic tariff rationalization in Union Budgets

concepts.name: WTO's Most Favoured Nation (MFN) Principle and Tariff Bindings
key_dimensions: MFN obligation: Any tariff advantage given to one member must be extended to all WTO members
Bound tariff rate vs. applied tariff rate — India's wide 'water' between the two and policy space implications
Exceptions to MFN: Regional Trade Agreements (GATT Article XXIV), GSP, and special provisions for LDCs
UPSC trap: MFN does NOT mean equal treatment to all countries in absolute terms — it means non-discrimination

concepts.name: Tariff Rate Quotas (TRQs)
key_dimensions: Mechanism: Lower tariff applied up to a quota threshold; higher (out-of-quota) tariff beyond it
Used in agriculture (WTO Agreement on Agriculture) as part of tariffication of non-tariff barriers
India's use of TRQs for sensitive agricultural commodities like maize, skimmed milk powder
UPSC trap: TRQs are NOT import quotas — they are tariff instruments with a quantity trigger

concepts.name: Anti-Dumping Duties: Definition, WTO Rules, and India's Usage
key_dimensions: Dumping defined: Exporting below normal value (domestic price or cost of production)
WTO Anti-Dumping Agreement: Three conditions — dumping margin, material injury, causal link
India as one of the world's largest users of anti-dumping measures — DGTR (formerly DGAD) role
UPSC trap: Anti-dumping duty is NOT a tariff in the traditional sense — it is a contingent/trade remedy measure, distinct from customs duty

concepts.name: Countervailing Duties (CVD) and Subsidies Agreement
key_dimensions: CVD imposed to offset foreign government subsidies that harm domestic industry
WTO SCM Agreement: Distinction between prohibited subsidies (red), actionable (yellow), and non-actionable (green — largely defunct)
Difference between CVD and anti-dumping duty: CVD targets government subsidy; AD targets firm-level pricing
UPSC trap: India's domestic CVD (under Customs Act) was used as a substitute for GST on imports — this has been restructured post-GST

concepts.name: Safeguard Measures under WTO: Temporary Protection Instrument
key_dimensions: Triggered by sudden surge in imports causing serious injury — NOT requiring proof of unfair trade practice
WTO Agreement on Safeguards: Four-year initial period, extendable to 8 years (10 for developing countries)
India's use of safeguard duties — solar cells case (domestic vs. imported solar panels controversy)
UPSC trap: Safeguards apply to ALL imports (MFN basis) unlike AD/CVD which are country/firm specific; and developing countries may be exempt below threshold

concepts.name: Non-Tariff Barriers (NTBs): Classification and WTO Disciplines
key_dimensions: UNCTAD classification: Technical measures (SPS, TBT), non-technical measures (quotas, licensing, price controls)
Distinction between legitimate regulatory measures and protectionist NTBs — the 'necessity test'
WTO disciplines: TBT Agreement and SPS Agreement as the primary frameworks governing NTBs
UPSC trap: Not all NTBs are WTO-illegal — the key is whether they are discriminatory or disguised restrictions

concepts.name: Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) Measures: Rules and Misuse
key_dimensions: SPS measures protect human, animal, plant health — must be based on scientific evidence and risk assessment
WTO SPS Agreement principles: Non-discrimination, scientific justification, precautionary principle (Article 5.7) — limited use
India facing SPS barriers: Shrimp/seafood exports to EU, mango exports ban — cases of developed country NTBs
UPSC trap: Precautionary principle under SPS is provisional and time-bound — NOT a permanent escape clause

concepts.name: Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT): Standards and Conformity Assessment
key_dimensions: TBT covers product standards, labeling, testing, certification requirements that can restrict trade
BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) mandatory certifications as both a legitimate standard and potential NTB
India's Quality Control Orders (QCOs) — surge since 2020 as a policy tool replacing tariffs post-WTO pressure
UPSC trap: TBT Agreement covers industrial goods; SPS covers food safety and animal/plant health — overlap in processed food products is a gray area

concepts.name: Import Licensing: Automatic vs. Non-Automatic Licensing
key_dimensions: WTO Import Licensing Agreement: Automatic licensing (for statistical purposes) vs. non-automatic (restricted items)
India's import licensing categories under DGFT: Free, Restricted, Canalized (through government agencies), Prohibited
Non-automatic licensing as a quantitative restriction — must be justified under GATT exceptions (Article XI, XX, XXI)
UPSC trap: Canalized imports (via STC, MMTC) are different from banned imports — they are state-trading restrictions, not prohibitions

concepts.name: Quantitative Restrictions (QRs) and India's WTO Disputes
key_dimensions: QRs (import quotas, bans) generally prohibited under GATT Article XI — unlike tariffs which are permitted
Exceptions: BoP reasons (Article XII/XVIII:B), national security (Article XXI), public morals/health (Article XX)
India-QRs case (1997-2001): US challenged India's QRs on 2,700 products maintained under BoP grounds — India lost
UPSC trap: India can reimpose QRs under BoP safeguards only when foreign exchange reserves are critically low — NOT for industrial protection

concepts.name: Rules of Origin: Preferential vs. Non-Preferential and Their Trade Policy Implications
key_dimensions: Rules of origin determine the 'nationality' of a product — critical for applying preferential tariffs under FTAs
Substantial transformation criteria: Change in tariff heading, value addition threshold (e.g., 35% in ASEAN FTA)
Problem of origin fraud and trade deflection — China routing goods through ASEAN to avail India's FTA benefits
UPSC trap: Non-preferential rules of origin (for MFN trade, labeling) are different from preferential rules — India has separate regulations for each

concepts.name: Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) and Reduction of Non-Tariff Costs
key_dimensions: TFA (2017, first multilateral agreement since WTO's founding): Aims to reduce border delays, customs red tape
Three categories: Category A (immediate), B (with transition period), C (with capacity building) — developing country flexibility
India's implementation: Single Window Interface for Facilitating Trade (SWIFT), ICEGATE, authorized economic operator program
UPSC trap: TFA reduces NTBs related to customs procedures but does NOT discipline product standards or SPS/TBT measures

concepts.name: Export Subsidies, Export Promotion Schemes, and WTO Compatibility
key_dimensions: WTO SCM Agreement prohibits export subsidies for non-agricultural goods for developed and (now) developing countries
India's schemes challenged by US: MEIS, SEZ, EOU, EPCGS — US argued India crossed $1,000 GNP per capita threshold
DS541 dispute (US vs. India): WTO ruled against India's export promotion schemes — India's response with RoDTEP, RoSCTL
UPSC trap: Agricultural export subsidies have a separate (more lenient) discipline under Agreement on Agriculture — not the same as industrial goods

concepts.name: Customs Valuation: WTO Agreement and Methods
key_dimensions: WTO Customs Valuation Agreement: Transaction value method is primary — the price actually paid or payable
Six methods in hierarchical order: Transaction value → identical goods → similar goods → deductive → computed → fall-back
Customs valuation disputes: Undervaluation by importers (especially from China) and India's use of 'reference prices'
UPSC trap: WTO Agreement eliminated arbitrary valuation methods — India cannot use 'official price lists' as primary valuation unless transaction value is rejected on defined grounds

concepts.name: Special and Differential Treatment (S&DT) for Developing Countries in Tariff Negotiations
key_dimensions: S&DT provisions allow developing countries longer implementation periods, lower reduction commitments, and policy space
Generalized System of Preferences (GSP): Developed countries voluntarily give preferential market access to developing countries — NOT legally binding
US withdrawal of India's GSP benefits (2019) — impact on Indian exports and India's counter-measures
UPSC trap: GSP is a unilateral, non-reciprocal preference — NOT an FTA; it can be withdrawn without WTO violation under the Enabling Clause

concepts.name: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) as an Emerging Non-Tariff Barrier
key_dimensions: EU's CBAM: Carbon price on imports from countries with less stringent climate policies — effective from 2026 for steel, cement, aluminium, fertilizers, electricity, hydrogen
India's concern: CBAM constitutes a disguised trade barrier and violates WTO principles of non-discrimination and common but differentiated responsibilities (CBDR)
WTO compatibility debate: Possible defense under GATT Article XX(b)/(g) — environmental exceptions

UPSC trap: CBAM is NOT a traditional tariff — it is a carbon pricing mechanism that functions like a tariff; India is developing a domestic carbon market (Carbon Credit Trading Scheme) partly in response

concepts.name: India's Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023: Key Instruments and Their Classification
key_dimensions: FTP 2023 key schemes: RoDTEP, RoSCTL, Advance Authorization, EPCG — distinction between duty remission and duty exemption schemes
Districts as Export Hubs, Towns of Export Excellence — decentralization of export promotion
Amnesty scheme for export obligation defaults — one-time settlement distinguishing FTP from customs law

UPSC trap: FTP is issued under Foreign Trade (Development & Regulation) Act, 1992 — NOT under Customs Act; DGFT administers FTP while CBIC administers customs — two separate authorities with overlapping jurisdiction on exports
